A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Act2Comm research work, including complete appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and results.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation results for Lucky Wheel, Catch the Ball, and Erratic Robot, together with complexity measurements and ablations in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulation results, complexity measurements, and ablations, including Figures 3–5 and 10–12 and Tables 3–6.

M1.justification: The Act2Comm architecture, quantizer, losses, critic-assisted training, and inference procedures in Section 5 and Appendix C are unchanged. The proof correction introduces no algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Lucky Wheel, Catch the Ball, and Erratic Robot environments, including the same deterministic and stochastic test scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods are unchanged, including the mechanism variants in Table 5 and Markov versus history-dependent coding in Figure 12a.

E3.justification: The BER and reward metrics, environment settings, model configurations, training settings, and testing procedures in Section 6 and Appendices C–E remain identical.

E4.justification: Both retain the same complexity, scalar-versus-vector representation, mechanism, feedback, message-length, and target-policy analyses in Appendices C and E.

E5.justification: Run-count and statistical reporting are unchanged, including averaging over 20,000 executions in Appendix D.1 and the 10,000 runs reported for complexity measurements in Appendix C.4.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are identical, including the BER–reward trade-offs, complexity measurements, and ablation outcomes in Figures 3–5 and 10–12 and Tables 3–6.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 corrects an entropy-derivation equality to an inequality, adds the corresponding upper-bound step in Equation 15, and explains equality under Markov policies. This locally repairs Theorem 1's proof; theorem statements, standing assumptions, and other theoretical results remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about channel capacity, the capacity–reward trade-off, and Act2Comm's practical communication capabilities.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the communication–reward trade-off, feedback benefits, scalability, and applicability remain unchanged. The added Markov-policy qualification concerns a formal proof step rather than revising these interpretations.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, pseudocode, and source-code and training-log access information are unchanged in Appendices C–D.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to implicit communication and finite-state channel research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds brief explanations of the corrected inequalities and a correction footnote. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 highlights the corrected mathematical steps in red, adds an equation line and footnote, and locally reflows pages 16–17, moving Equation 16 onto page 17. Figures and tables are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 asserts a general equality where v3 uses an upper bound and explains its tightness under Markov policies (Appendix B.1, Equation 15). This improves the accuracy and transparency of the capacity proof, while leaving the main conclusions, method, and empirical evidence unchanged.
